meaning: The pulsatile run is drawn first so it sits underneath the mean-level run, and the comment asserts that at RUN_ALPHA = 0.85 the pulsatile envelope still reads as one band while the traces on top of it stay visible. This is a layering/legibility claim about draw order and alpha, not a change to any simulated quantity.

could_move.what: Any deck that overlays a pulsatile run with a mean-level run: the pulsatile band goes from covering to being covered, so which trace is readable flips.
Dual-axis pressure panels specifically, where the comment says the pulsatile envelope previously covered everything else.
The m5-vs-patient decks that pair the two runs, e.g. jugular_compression_m5_vs_p081 and the p083/p137/p150 siblings.
jugular_compression_m5_vs_data, which the comment says is the same deck superseded by _m5_vs_p<patient>, so it may still render with the older order.
_m3_vs_m5, which needs an m3 export in the same jugular_compression folder, so it may not rebuild cleanly to check the claim.

expectation: No change to solved values. Visual only: the pulsatile envelope moves behind the mean trace. Whether "traces inside it stay visible" holds at alpha 0.85 depends on the panel and cannot be judged from the code alone — on dense dual-axis panels it may still obscure. I cannot tell without looking at the rendered figures.

check.why: Replots one patient deck that pairs the pulsatile and mean-level runs, without re-fitting, so the layering and the 0.85 alpha claim can be inspected directly on the dual-axis pressure panels.
